items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to the membership
of the New York state housing finance agency, the housing trust fund
corporation and the affordable housing corporation
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7757

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to the
membership of the New York state housing finance agency, the housing
trust fund corporation and the affordable housing corporation

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to expand the NYS HFA membership to include
one director appointed by the temporary president of the Senate, and one
director appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly.  Further, it aligns
membership of the NYS HFA with its subsidiary corporations, the Housing
Trust Fund Corporation and the Affordable Housing Corporation.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends subdivision 1 of Section 43 of the Private Housing
Finance Law to include within the composition of the NYS HFA, one direc-
tor appointed by the Temporary President of the Senate and one director
appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly. The directors appointed by the
Temporary President of the Senate and the Speaker of the Assembly shall
serve at the pleasure of the Temporary President of the Senate and the
Speaker of the Assembly respectively. Any vacancy shall be filled, for
the unexpired term, if applicable, in the same manner as the original
appointment.

Section two amends subdivision 3 of section 45-a of the Private Housing
Finance Law to align the board composition of the Housing Trust Fund
Corporation with the Housing Finance Agency.

Section three amends subdivision 3 of section 45-b of the Private Hous-
ing Finance Law to align the board composition of the Affordable Housing
Corporation with the Housing Finance Agency.

Section four sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Housing Finance Agency (HFA) is a public benefit corporation. Its
membership consists of the Commissioner of the Division of Housing and
Community Renewal (DHCR), the Director of the Budget, the Commissioner
of Taxation and Finance, and four members appointed by the Governor with
the advice and consent of the Senate. The Housing Trust Fund Corporation
(HTFC) and the Affordable Housing Corporation (AHC) are both subsidiary
corporations of HFA. Currently, the membership of the HTFC includes the
Commissioner of DHCR (who serves as Chair), the Chair of HFA and one
additional member appointed by the Chair of the HTFC. The membership of
the Affordable Housing Corporation includes members of HFA as may be
constituted from time to time, and the Chair of HFA. To allow for great-
er efficiency and accountability in the administration of the State's
housing resources, this bill would expand membership of HFA to provide
for Senate and Assembly appointees and align membership of the HTFC and
AHC with that of the HFA.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S.2254 (Little) - Referred to Housing, Construction, and Community
Development

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None to the State

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of January next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become law.
